Steyning Grammar School and Sixth Form College is a unique, successful and dynamic learning community, offering day and State Boarding for students from ages 11-18. Our ‘Journey to Excellence’ is built on traditions of excellence and highest expectations, combined with a commitment to innovation and new thinking – to support our students in being the best they can be in preparation for their exciting futures.
My name is Kate Armstrong, I’m in year 12 and I’ve been part of the Steyning Grammar School family for four years now.
I have really enjoyed my three years so far at SGS, I have taken part in my fair share of clubs and have enjoyed all of them.
What I have loved about my three years so far at SGS are the brilliant resources and facilities. For example, I really enjoy the library at shooting field, which has a range of books and ebooks (which I can read on my iPad at home and at school).

pageCache.pageTitle: Maths - Steyning Grammar School Steyning Grammar School
pageCache.text:
Maths
At Steyning Grammar School we intend to deliver a rich and challenging Mathematics curriculum that encourages an enjoyment of the subjects, and enables students to recognise the value of Mathematics and the skills associated with it. We want every student to find every lesson both engaging and challenging. Our approach is that all students can achieve and progress within our subject, and we aim for students to leave SGS with a strong mathematical understanding and a positive attitude towards the subject . The fundamentals of our curriculum are underpinned by four key principles:
Fluency – we aim to develop fluent mathematicians, who are able to recall and apply their knowledge to a variety of problems. This is underpinned by a strong foundation built upon from KS2, with an initial focus on the fundamental Numeracy skills in KS3, and embedded through continuous practice across their school career developing their grit.
Reasoning – our students are able to reason mathematically, and make connections between different areas of mathematics, developing their curiosity in the process. The introduction of increasingly complex problems over time enables students to develop a conceptual understanding.
Mathematical communication – students are able to communicate both ideas and solutions. They are able to use mathematical vocabulary in the relevant situations and can communicate ideas through extended methods and working. The Numeracy skills developed throughout their school career are continually used and extended.
Problem solving – from the start of KS3, students are exposed to and able to approach both routine and non-routine problem solving questions. Approaches to problems are developed, including the ability to break down longer problems into isolated smaller calculations, and recognising the application of multiple areas of Mathematics. We encourage our students to show creativity in their approaches to problem solving.
A ‘game-changing’ student in Maths is:
A student who demonstrates inquiry, explores independently the mathematical concepts being taught and makes sound logical steps when problem solving. Game changers in Maths have an innate drive to explore the mathematical world around them and see how it connects, influences and supports other disciplines. Maths game changers demonstrate their passion for the subject in and outside the classroom, reviewing and reflecting on ideas that turn into hypotheses to help us understand the world. Maths game changers are always curious.

pageCache.text:
Science
Scientific understanding is changing our lives and is vital to the world’s future prosperity, and all students should be taught essential aspects of knowledge, methods, processes and uses of science.
We must provide opportunities for students to critically evaluate information and to form their own opinions so that they are able to explore and evaluate the changing world around them.
Finally, our curriculum should engage all learners and make them “gamechangers” through increasing their science capital and enable them to be successful​, so they have the desire to continue studying science post 16. Scientifically-minded students will be better prepared to instigate and build on the changes of the future.
Biology Learning Journey
Chemistry Learning Journey
Physics Learning Journey
A ‘game-changing’ student in Science is:
A student who demonstrates an intense level of curiosity in science, making intuitive leaps in solving science problems. Game changers in science work hard on achieving an extensive knowledge base and are able to relate that knowledge to new problems and topics. Game changers demonstrate unusually high levels of motivation and/or concentration and an ability to integrate information and concepts into existing knowledge schemas. Science game changers persist, showing grit, in the pursuit of attempting to comprehend abstract concepts beyond age level expectations and want to see connections between science and the world around them, using mathematics to understand, define and or solve problems.
Albert Einstein: ‘The important thing is not to stop questioning. Curiosity has its own reason for existing.’

pageCache.pageTitle: Careers and Guidance - Steyning Grammar School Steyning Grammar School
pageCache.text:
Careers and Guidance
Our careers team provide high quality careers education, information, advice and guidance (CEIAG) to motivate and inspire our students. We aim to equip them with the skills, knowledge and information needed to achieve their full potential at school, work, and ultimately throughout their career.
The careers programme is structured, impartial and embedded across the whole school. We adhere to statutory guidance and careers education, including “Careers Guidance and Access for Education and Training Providers” and work closely with the Careers and Enterprise Company to ensure compliance with relevant legislation.
We also use the Gatsby charitable foundation’s benchmarks to develop and improve our careers provision. Find out more here: Good Careers Guidance Report
The Gatsby benchmarks ensure that we are providing an outstanding programme of support to our students that is regularly reviewed to national standards.
Throughout our careers programme we collaborate with employers and post-16/18 learning providers including local colleges, 6th forms universities and apprenticeship training providers. An independent careers adviser provides careers interviews ensuring every student receives bespoke support before they leave the school. We also work with other organisations that aim to support young people in theirtransition from the school into further learning or the workplace, including the local authority and National Careers Service.
Where possible providers are invited into school to work with students through collapsed timetable days, events, assemblies, tutor sessions and targeted group work.
If you would like to learn more about our careers program learn more about how to get involved, please email: careers@sgs.uk.net.
We are thrilled to work with Claire Jewel as our Enterprise Adviser.
Careers Lead – Sarah Linsdell slinsdell@sgs.uk.net
Careers Adviser – Marie Harding- mharding@sgs.uk.net
Measuring success
Reviewing impact is a key part of what we do. Our careers programme is organic-it grows and changes with each cohort to ensure we are meeting the needs of students and providing relevant activities to help them shape their futures.
We work closely with the local authority providing destinations data (also reported to our governors) and to provide intervention for students at risk of becoming NEET (not in education, employment, or training).
We regularly evaluate all our workshops and events asking both students and providers to share their views in order to gauge the impact and him prove provision. Students’ progress is further reviewed using the Unifrog and skills builder toolkits, as well as future skills questionnaire to examine provision and impact across their time at Steyning Grammar School. This data, along with feedback from parents and carers feeds into our annual action plans.We formally assess our progress towards each of the 8 Gatsby benchmarks each term using the composite valuation tool as part of our partnership working with the Careers andEnterprise Company.
Our next review will be December 2026
Unifrog
We are now using the Unifrog Careers Software across the whole school. All students in all year groups have been sent a link to make an account and this they can use at home and at school. Unifrog is a “one-stop-shop” online platform for secondary school students in the UK, helping them explore interests, discover post-school opportunities (universities, apprenticeships, colleges), and manage applications for their best next step after school, providing tools for writing personal statements, CVs, and recording achievements for teachers and counsellors too.
If our parent/carers would like to have access to their student’s Unifrog then please email us and will can set this up for you. We shall be using Unifrog for all work experience provision in Year 10 and Year 12 as well.
-For a parent/carer guide to Post-16 Options click here
Careers in the curriculum
Teaching staff and departments are aware of their important role in careers. Careers content is embedded into lessons and staff are actively working towards improving the careers inthe curriculum content for their subject. Within tutor time we have a dedicated session every two weeks where we focus on careers in different subject areas, including labour market information and essential skills required by employers.
Resources to support provision for teachers:
CEC: My Learning My FutureLSIP – Local Skills Improvement PlanCAREERS Hub Resources Library
All staff also have access to Unifrog so that they can share labour market information (LMI) with students using the careers library tool.
We encourage all staff to consider careers learning opportunities when running trips and events-such as “making every trip a careers trip”, by requesting speakers to share their careers journeys and experiences whilst on the trip.

pageCache.pageTitle: Careers Guidance - Steyning Grammar School Steyning Grammar School
pageCache.text:
Careers Guidance
All students have access to the careers software used across the school, which contains careers information, including pay scales, videos about the roles and routes into employment. The school currently uses Kudos for this purpose from home and school and all students can access the National Careers Website.
In year 8 students take a careers and pathways project. This looks at a range of careers and the routes into them tracing the journey back to smart choices at options time for GCSEs to A level and on to uni, apprenticeship etc. During the project the students put on a careers fair getting the opportunity to present about careers that they are interested in while learning from others about their choices. The whole project is further supported by visiting Alumni who come into lessons to talk about their own careers and the experiences and journey that led them to where they are today. Students find this fascinating. The project is designed to help students informed choices and hopefully relieve some of the anxiety about making decisions.
During PSHE lessons Year 9 explore what it is like to be an employee, reviewing their rights and responsibilities. In this changing world, it is important that they realise the different types of contract that they could be employed on, including zero hours contracts and the benefits and pitfalls within these. We also review equal opportunities and what this means within the workplace and employment law. This helps them build an understanding of what they can expect within the workplace
In Year 10 PSHE students review themselves and the skills and qualities they have building a portfolio to identify the type of person they are and the types of careers which might suit them. This is explored through a number of questionnaires and quizzes, to help them prepare for their next choices after Year 11. Some students will have their 1 – 1 careers discussion with the Careers Team in this year.
All students have a 1 – 1 careers discussion where they not only consider their next step into apprenticeships, further education colleges and 6th form colleges, but look further afield into their future career plans and what they want to go onto post 18, for example university and apprenticeships. Follow up meetings are hosted with the students to support with applications and CV building as necessary. During the first term of PSHE students have a number of visiting speakers to look further into their choices. These sessions look at 6th form colleges, further education colleges, university and apprenticeships. We have visiting Alumni who share their experiences with the students so to support them in making informed choices. Students are encouraged to drop in to our Careers Surgery, to ask questions during break and lunch times for any additional support, this is available all year round.

Art and Photography
Autonomous learners are able to independently adapt and exploit a variety of skills, both practical and critical.
Resilient students will be confident to take risks and comfortable with ambiguity whilst experimenting with visual language.
Thinking critically and creatively when responding to an awakened understanding of the world through and appreciation of art and culture.
Art and photography Learning Journey
A ‘game-changing’ student in Art is:
A student who explores the creative world outside the classroom by visiting galleries, reading books, watching documentaries and creating art. A student who can make connections between their own work and the work of other artists. A student who takes risks, exploring a range of ideas and media and always pushing their own ideas, reviewing and reflecting as they work. A student who understands the connection between art and the world around them.
Photography Learning Journey
A ‘game-changing’ student in Photography is:
A student who independently researches different media, techniques and photographers by reading relevant articles, watching documentaries, visiting galleries and exhibitions. They then use this information to influence their own photography practice. A student who is fearless in pushing the boundaries of the photographic process and taking risks.

pageCache.pageTitle: PE, Dance, Food: Curriculum - Steyning Grammar School Steyning Grammar School
pageCache.text:
PE, Dance, Food: Curriculum
A ‘game-changing’ student in PE is an individual who is passionate about engaging in a wide range of sports. They are eager to enhance their performance from technical, tactical, and physical fitness standpoints. Game Changers in PE are also enthusiastic about understanding the theoretical aspects of sport and performance. They are eager to expand their knowledge of the physiological, psychological, and socio-cultural components of Physical Education.
Skill development / showcase skills
Life long participation
Develop student’s character
Developing theoretical knowledge, that underpins practical performance
P.E. Learning Journey
A ‘game changing student’ in Food is a student who is passionate about all aspects of food. They enjoy the creativity of playing around with flavours and presentation to give a WOW factor to a dish. They are someone that enjoys to cook in their own time, and contribute to the creative world by getting enthused by documentaries and cooking programs about food, reading books, trialling and adapting recipes for improvement. A ‘game changing’ food student will want to be involved in any food experiences; including learning from visiting chiefs and taking part in competitions both in and out of a school setting.
A ‘game-changing’ student in Dance is:
A student who fully engages in the world of dance, watching and learning from professionals in all genres. Someone who appreciates dance as an art form and not just entertainment. Game changer dance students can apply corrections quickly, absorb movement and direction and have the ability to think ahead as they dance. They are supportive and encouraging of their class mates and show up rather than show off. Game changer dance students also have a profound sense of musicality and rhythm with a love of interpreting music. Choreographically, game changers are creative and use artistry and self expression to engage with an audience and generate an emotive response.
“I don’t want people who want to dance, I want people who have to dance” George Balanchine

pageCache.pageTitle: Design Technology - Steyning Grammar School Steyning Grammar School
pageCache.text:
Design Technology
Design and technology is an inspiring, rigorous and practical subject. Using creativity and imagination, pupils design and make products that solve real and relevant problems within a variety of contexts, considering their own and others’ needs, wants and values. They acquire a broad range of subject knowledge and draw on disciplines such as mathematics, science, engineering, computing and art.
The Key Stage 3 Technology curriculum map at Steyning covers four different technologies. These are taught in rotation to allow all students best access to the rooms. They do not need to be sequential as the skills and theory build over the two years and are revisited. KS3 is designed to lay the foundation for KS4 which in turn leads to Product design at KS5. BET Assessments take place in November or January for KS3. The tests are created with a focus on the Design Process. Project work is self evaluated, peer assessed and with teachers giving the final feedback.
Cultural Capital/British Values/SMSC:
Design Technology Learning Journey
A ‘game changing’ student in DT is a student who engages with many of the world’s current complex issues. Learning how to make a positive impact, thus quelling anxiety and enabling positive action for the greater good. The student who develops the ability to problem solve in a creative way, thinking differently to everyone else. The student who actively contributes to the creativity, culture, wealth and well-being of themselves, their community and the world as a whole. The student who takes risks and so becomes more resourceful, innovative, enterprising and capable. The student who sees the subject as a transformative pedagogy that has the potential to deliver on the very challenges we face today – revelling in the immersive experience while learning; making mistakes and trying over and over again.

pageCache.pageTitle: R.E. - Steyning Grammar School Steyning Grammar School
pageCache.text:
R.E.
The Citizenship and RE curriculum at SGS equips students for life beyond school, through critically engaging with religious scripture in the context of the social, political and cultural issues in today’s world.
Through our core RE and citizenship provision, we want to develop empathetic, religiously literate, well-rounded individuals who are responsible global citizens who are empowered to be the gamechangers in today’s world.
Students will develop a respect for others and have the opportunity to reflect upon their own beliefs. The engaging curriculum provides an opportunity for students to grow socially, spiritually, morally and culturally.
R.E. Learning Journey
A game-changing student in RE develops a respect for others and uses opportunities to reflect upon their own beliefs. These students are able to explain the way in which people engage in the world: socially, spiritually, morally and culturally. These students are empathetic, religiously literate, well-rounded individuals who are responsible global citizens; empowered to be the gamechangers in today’s world.
